verified_key_information_units.information: AS Tallinna Vesi reported strong financial performance in 2025 with revenue increasing 11.4% to €72.48 million, operating profit rising 11.8% to €21.22 million, and net profit growing 7.2% to €14.24 million. The company invested €55.74 million in fixed assets.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Main financial indicators table; Statement of comprehensive income

candidate_sentences.text: Tallinna Vesi reported robust financial performance for 2025, characterized by significant revenue growth and improved profitability.
Total sales increased by 11.4% to €72.48 million, up from €65.08 million in the previous year.
Profitability metrics strengthened considerably during the period.
Gross profit rose by 10.5% to €29.52 million, while operating profit increased by 11.8% to €21.22 million.
Net profit grew by 7.2% to €14.24 million, resulting in earnings per share of €0.71.
Investments in fixed assets reached €55.74 million, exceeding the previous year’s €49.53 million, focusing on infrastructure continuity, environmental protection, and smart meter installations.

verified_key_information_units.information: Customer revenue mix shifted significantly due to regulatory tariff harmonization: private customer sales increased 18.3% to €31.84 million from higher consumption, while business customer sales decreased 2.7% to €16.76 million following reduced tariff rates for businesses.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Sales section breakdown tables and text

candidate_sentences.text: This growth was driven primarily by an 18.3% rise in sales to private customers in the main service area, reaching €31.84 million, which was supported by increased consumption and tariff adjustments implemented throughout 2024 and 2025.
Conversely, sales to business customers declined by 2.7% to €16.76 million, reflecting a statutory reduction in water tariff rates for this segment aimed at harmonizing prices with private customers.

verified_key_information_units.information: Cost optimization and energy transition efforts reduced electricity expenses through the new combined heat and power plant at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, which supplied 43.8% of site electricity needs and increased renewable energy consumption to 87% of total energy use (from 23% in 2020).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Energy use and energy consumption overview section

candidate_sentences.text: The improvement in operating margins was largely attributable to cost optimizations, particularly the reduction in electricity expenses following the full operational capacity of the combined heat and power plant at the Paljassaare Wastewater Treatment Plant.
This facility now generates all the heat and more than half of the electricity required for treatment processes, significantly lowering purchased energy costs.

verified_key_information_units.information: Infrastructure modernization advanced with smart water meter rollout covering over 80% of customers (targeting 100% by end-2026), construction of 45.1 km of pipes (49% via trenchless methods), and launch of trenchless sewer rehabilitation service by subsidiary Watercom renewing approximately 6 km of pipes.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Investing for the Future; Watercom activities

verified_key_information_units.information: The company achieved 99.5% compliance with drinking water quality standards and was awarded 'Green Company of the Year'. Environmental initiatives included constructing 7.1 km of separate stormwater systems to reduce flooding and setting ambitious climate targets to reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% from 2020 levels by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2040.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Highlights from 2025; Sustainability Statement; Climate change section

verified_key_information_units.information: The group maintained a strong liquidity position with €11.29 million cash balance at year-end and €160 million outstanding loans carrying an average interest rate of 3.24%. In December 2025, €5 million was drawn under a €25 million loan agreement with the Nordic Investment Bank to support future investments.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of financial position; Investors section

candidate_sentences.text: The company’s debt levels increased, with outstanding loans rising to €160 million from €118 million at the end of 2024, leading to a debt-to-total-assets ratio of 66.02%.
Despite the increased leverage, the company maintained a healthy liquidity position with cash balances growing to €11.29 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Tallinna Vesi continued its dividend policy of distributing 50-80% of annual profit, paying €0.53 per share (80% of 2024 net profit) to shareholders in June 2025, balancing returns with investment needs.

candidate_sentences.text: The company also continued its commitment to shareholder returns, having paid a dividend of €0.53 per share in 2025, representing 80% of the 2024 net profit.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key 2026 strategic priorities include completing the smart meter rollout, harmonizing water tariffs for residential and commercial customers by summer 2026, advancing the ozonation project at Ülemiste water treatment plant, reconstructing secondary clarifiers at Paljassaare wastewater treatment plant, and executing planned investments of up to €60 million.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K6, and K7 are fully present with supporting sentences. K4 and K5 are missing entirely, as there is no mention of infrastructure modernization details, water quality compliance, environmental initiatives, or climate targets. K8 is also missing, as there is no reference to 2026 strategic priorities. The overall coverage is mixed, with strong representation of financial performance, customer revenue mix, cost optimization, and liquidity but significant omissions in infrastructure, environmental, and strategic planning details, leading to a Neutral/Mixed score.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected, with clear cause-and-effect relationships (e.g., tariff adjustments driving private customer sales growth, cost optimizations improving margins). The structure progresses logically from revenue performance to profitability, balance sheet, operational metrics, and shareholder returns. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational problems. While there is a minor numerical relationship between segment sales and total sales (private + business + construction = €56.06m vs. total €72.48m), the candidate does not claim these are exhaustive additive components of the same total, and segment figures may include inter-segment transactions or different scopes as permitted by the accounting safeguard. No unnecessary repetition materially reduces clarity.
